$comment: P0-06 — the certified main-branch protection contract for the Bizosto marketing website.
This is the website half of the certification whose ERP half lives in
lacreativodesign/nextjs-boilerplate. The two are deliberately SEPARATE files verified by
SEPARATE workflows, each running inside the repository it certifies, under that
repository's own job token.
That separation is the point. This repository is CURRENTLY PUBLIC only as a temporary
GitHub Free-plan expedient, while the certified final posture is PRIVATE. Once that private
posture is restored, a job token issued to the ERP repository cannot read this repository
and GitHub answers 404. A cross-repository read that fails must never be reported as a
successful certification, so neither repository vouches for the other.
It holds no credential.
STILL OPEN, AND STILL DELIBERATE — the ruleset existing does not close this.
The live ruleset now enforces everything else, but required_approving_review_count is
0 because this repository has exactly ONE account with any access, and that account
authors every pull request. GitHub does not let an author approve their own, so raising
the count to 1 would not add a review - it would stop anything merging.
Closing it is a two-step owner action, in this order, never the second alone:
1. grant a second human WRITE access to THIS repository (the ERP repository needs
its own separate collaborator; they do not share one);
2. set required_approving_review_count to 1 AND set certifiedFloor to 1 here.
gapOpen keeps step 2 honest: the certification suite refuses to let it go false while
certifiedFloor is still 0, so the gap cannot be closed on paper alone.
The Vercel app's deployment status. Reports as a commit STATUS, not a check run.
Integration id 8329 is pinned: a context can be re-pointed at a different app while
keeping its name, which would satisfy a name-only check with a report this repository
never produces.
GitHub Actions - the `dependency-security` job in
.github/workflows/dependency-security.yml, added by PR #61 and merged to main on
2026-09-17 at 632f5daf6e5981dd610b59199c7230f38b8cd2c0. It runs `npm ci` then
`npm run security:audit`, which is `npm audit --audit-level=high`, so it fails on ANY
high or critical advisory across the whole lockfile including dev dependencies.
It is LIVE, not future work: the owner added it to ruleset 23581080 as a second
required status check, and it ran green on main after the merge (run 35264726041,
job 105348912555). PR #61 brought the repository to 0 critical and 0 high.
The workflow is deliberately NOT path-filtered. A required check that is skipped for
pull requests touching unrelated files leaves GitHub waiting on it forever, which
would block every such merge - the same dead-required-check failure mode this
certification checks for elsewhere.
Integration id 15368 is GitHub Actions and is pinned for the same reason as Vercel.
A check called `dependency-security` posted by anything else does not satisfy this.
BOTH of these are required on the live ruleset, and both were read back from
GET /repos/lacreativodesign/bizosto-website/rulesets/23581080 on 2026-09-17. The live
required_status_checks list contains exactly these two contexts and no others.
Losing either one is P0-06 drift, and so is re-pointing either at a different
integration. The contract is DIRECTIONAL, so the owner may add further required checks
without failing this record - but these two may never disappear.
APPLIED AND LIVE as of 2026-09-17: ruleset 23581080, read back by direct authenticated
GET and verified field by field, including bypass_actors being explicitly present and
empty and current_user_can_bypass being "never". It is the only ruleset on the
repository.
THE RULESET CONTROL IS GREEN, AND IT NOW CARRIES TWO REQUIRED CHECKS.
Vercel/8329 and dependency-security/15368. The second arrived with PR #61, which was
merged to main on 2026-09-17 (632f5daf6e5981dd610b59199c7230f38b8cd2c0) and brought the
repository to 0 critical and 0 high advisories. The owner then added it to the ruleset,
so the dependency audit is branch-blocking rather than advisory.
TWO OTHER CONTROLS ARE STILL OPEN.
1. VISIBILITY - OPEN. This repository is currently PUBLIC. It was published so the
ruleset could be created at all: GitHub Free serves rulesets on public repositories
only, and the owner cannot upgrade right now. That is a temporary expedient and NOT
the target state - this repository holds proprietary Bizosto marketing source and
must end up PRIVATE.
expectedVisibility therefore stays "private", and the verifier reports the current
public state as repository.visibility DRIFT. That failure is correct and intended; it
must not be silenced by changing the expectation. The owner action is to upgrade to
GitHub Pro or higher, make the repository private, and then re-verify that the ruleset
survived the visibility change.
2. INDEPENDENT REVIEW - OPEN. See requiredApprovingReviewCount above. Another account the
owner personally controls does not close this: P0-06 asks for INDEPENDENT review, and
an account under the same control is not independent.
Because rulesetId is recorded, the verifier pins the read to that id rather than
discovering the ruleset by name.
